content.title: About
content.content: Crackers are dry, crunchy baked products made from flour, water and a small amount of fat. They are often enjoyed as a light snack or as an accompaniment to soups, salads and cheeses. The water in the dough provides the necessary moisture and helps create the characteristic porous texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Crackers appeared in Europe in the 19th century as a lighter alternative to bread.
There are many varieties: wheat, rye, corn and gluten‑free flours are used.
Crackers are a staple in military rations because of their long shelf life.
In some countries they are served with cheese, cold cuts or pâté as a "tapas" style snack.
Thin crackers can be flavored with herbs, spices or cheese.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Most crackers contain little fat and calories, making them a convenient snack for weight management.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: The flour provides slowly released energy, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain versions are rich in dietary fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: Pairs well with protein
items.content: Crackers are often served with cheese, ham or nut spreads, enhancing their nutritional profile.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Water in the recipe helps maintain optimal product moisture and aids nutrient absorption.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some crackers are high in salt, which may be unsuitable for people with hypertension.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat‑based crackers are not suitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Recipes may contain dairy, soy or nuts, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: If stored too long, crackers can become soft or stale, so checking the expiration date is important.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Crackers can be eaten plain, spread with cream cheese, hummus, pâté, or used as a base for canapés. They are commonly served alongside soups, salads and cheeses. For best flavor, keep them in a dry place.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store crackers in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For extended storage, keep them in the refrigerator to prevent moisture buildup and spoilage.
